references.text: This verse is the positive counterpart to the curse - blessed when you come in and go out, which stands in contrast to the curse in verse 19.
Moses speaks of going out and coming in, using the same language that describes daily activities and movements.
The Lord will keep your coming in and your going out - uses the same expression, but in the context of God's protection instead of a curse.
The phrase 'go out and come in' is used regarding leadership and daily activity in Israel.
Caleb describes his strength to go out and come in, which refers to all of life's activities.
A parallel curse about being cursed in the city and in the field, part of the same series of curses.
